value.body: A chef prepares food in a hotel, restaurant, catering or cruise kitchen, working within a section such as pastry, Indian or continental. Hotels, restaurants, caterers and cruise lines hire chefs. A typical shift is preparation, cooking during service and cleaning down, often on evenings, weekends and holidays.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BHM, a B.Sc in Hospitality, or a culinary diploma

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join through campus placement or a kitchen trial as a commis chef, or through a hotel's culinary training programme. Food safety training such as FSSAI's FoSTaC certificate is commonly expected.

value.title: At a glance
items: Typical path: commis, demi chef de partie, chef de partie, sous chef, executive chef.
Long hours and physical work are normal, especially early on.
Some later move into catering, food production or their own outlet.
